text:
maya: Heads-up — after the int4 rollout for buttercup14b we're seeing a 15-30% p50 latency increase on short prompts (<=50 tokens). Not traffic-wide but noticeable on the low-latency cohort.

alex: How big is p95? Any error spikes or OOMs?

maya: p95 is up ~20-35ms depending on region. No new OOMs, error rate flat. GPU util is similar but kernel latency histogram shows a new long tail on attention kernel. Snippet from perf tracer:```
ATTN_KERNEL: mean 3.2ms -> 5.1ms, 99p 9ms -> 18ms
KV_PREFETCH: spikes aligning with attn stalls
```

sam: Were we using prefetch + small batch sizes? Those two combo can blow up kernel scheduling. What were batching/window settings for the canary?

maya: Canary config: `batch.max_tokens=4096`, `batch.max_batch_size=8`, `prefetch.window=3`, `kv.prefetch=true`. Canary was ~10% traffic on dc-west.

jin: My hunch: int4 codepath is causing extra ops that interact poorly with our slab allocator and prefetch ordering. Memory compaction not triggered fast enough so kernels occasionally fall back to slower path. We saw similar with orion2b. Try disabling prefetch or shrinking window first.

alex: Agree — quick experiments to try: 1) Disable kv.prefetch for int4 only 2) Reduce prefetch.window=1 3) Increase slab_alignment/reserve (e.g. `slab.reserve_mb=16`) 4) Compare int8 vs int4 latency with same batching.

maya: I'm starting an A/B run now. Quick command for reproducible bench:```
./tools/perf_run.sh --model=buttercup14b --quant=int4 --prompt-tokens=32 --iters=400 --batch-size=1
./tools/perf_run.sh --model=buttercup14b --quant=int8 --prompt-tokens=32 --iters=400 --batch-size=1
```

sam: Also try microbatching: set `batch.max_batch_size=4` and `max_tokens_per_batch=2048` so we avoid tiny batches hitting perf cliffs. Might reduce p50.

jin: If that doesn't move it, try the kernel-affinity change we discussed: `kernel.bind_cpu=1` for the attn kernel to avoid context jitter. We had a patch for that in staging.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout status: int4 buttercup14b -> 10% started @3267891200, metric alerts triggered @3267891230, automatically stepped down to 2% at 3267891245.

maya: Results from quick A/B (first 200 iters): int8 p50=42ms, int4 p50=55ms. When I turned off kv.prefetch for int4 p50 dropped to 46ms. p95 improved similarly.

alex: Interesting — suggests prefetch ordering interacts badly with int4 path. Do we have perf traces to show exact op ordering differences?

maya: Attached perf traces in the experiment bucket (s3://ri-perf/buttercup14b/int4-prefetch-326789). Key takeaway: several `kv_prefetch` ops issued earlier for int4, causing overlap and extra memcpy GC.

sam: For immediate mitigation we should: 1) revert prefetch default for buttercup14b int4 2) set temporary model-specific default `prefetch.window=1` 3) lower default `generation.max_new_tokens` from 128->64 for this model to keep short prompt cohort in a safe latency envelope while we root cause.

jin: I'll prototype slab reserve and kernel-affinity patches in a branch and run soak. If that reduces the tail it's a candidate for rollout.

maya: Agreed. I'll open a small deploy PR to pin buttercup14b int4 prefetch=false and change model-defaults: `max_new_tokens=64` and `batch.max_batch_size=4` for the canary.

alex: Sounds good. Can we also add a short eval for quality delta int8 vs int4 at those gen settings? Don't want to regress user-facing quality while we tune latency.

maya: On it — running eval set A (conversational+completion) with the two configs. Will post results once complete.

sam: Assign me to follow-up: I'll run long-run soak with slab reserve=16 and kernel-affinity to see if fragmentation is the root cause.

maya: Thanks everyone. Plan summary: (1) revert/limit prefetch for int4 buttercup14b, (2) temp model defaults: max_new_tokens=64, batch.size=4, (3) run bench+eval, (4) Jin to prototype allocator/kernel fixes. If anybody wants to help with bench runs ping me. :pray:
